Items.Authors: Christopher S. Benson
Items.Title: Performance characterisation of the 2026-2027 South Pole Telescope Shirokoff Line Intensity Mapper on-chip spectrometers
Items.Abstract: After its first engineering run in the 2024-2025 Austral Summer observing season, the South Pole Telescope - Shirokoff Line Intensity Mapper (SPT-SLIM) has undergone design and fabrication iterations to improve the resolution of its on-chip spectrometers and the sensitivity of its kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) in preparation for its next observing season (2026-2027). In this effort, we have investigated low-loss amorphous silicon dielectrics coupled with implementations of the SPT-SLIM KIDs with parallel plate capacitors and lower inductor volumes. Additionally, we have developed a parallel fabrication process to our efforts at Argonne National Laboratories through Cardiff University and other fabrication facilities in the UK. We present high-resolution spectral response measurements coupled with general performance measurements for the new generation of SPT-SLIM spectrometers, comparing both our fabrication tracks and also against the previous deployment spectrometers.

Items.Authors: Charlotte Braithwaite, Giampaolo Pisano, Carole Tucker, Richard Lewis, Rashmikant Sudiwala, Ian Veenendaal, Peter Hargrave
Items.Title: Performance of metal mesh half wave plates designed for sub-mm studies
Items.Abstract: Experimental characterisation of polarisation modulators prior to installation in telescopes is essential to understand their performance and identify any issues arising from the design and manufacturing process. Previously, experiments have only included on-axis measurements, however, it is also important to measure the performance at the extreme off-axis angles of incidence due to changes that may arise in the performance of the device. With future wide-field sub-mm instruments planning to include metal mesh HWPs as polarisation modulators it is essential to characterise the off-axis performance for this type of device.  In this report we describe the methodology and present results for on- and off- axis measurements of a prototype metal mesh HWP designed for CMB studies. We present initial findings which indicate a dependency on the orientation of which side of the HWP is presented to the sky first and discuss further work required to account for any signal losses.

Items.Authors: Matthew J. Lehner, Shiang-Yu Wang, Joel Castro-Chacon, Zhi-Wei Zhang, Chung-Kai Huang, Mauricio Reyes-Ruiz, Wei-Ling Yen, Yin-Chang Chang, Bo-Jhou Wang, Chueh-Yi Chou, J.J. Kavelaars, Benjamin Hernandez-Valencia, Liliana Figueroa, Ivan Zavala-Ibarra, Tomas Calvario Velásquez, Javier Hernandez-Landa, Charles Alcock, Andrew Szentgyorgyi, Tim Norton, John Geary, Jennifer Karr, Sharon Goliath, John Ouellette
Items.Title: Performance of the Transneptunian Automated Occultation Survey (TAOS II)
Items.Abstract: The Transneptunian Automated Occultation Survey (TAOS II) aims to measure the size distribution of small (D ~ 1 km) Trans-Neptunian Objects. Such objects are very faint (r' > 40) and are undetectable by even the largest telescopes. TAOS II is a blind survey, designed to simultaneously monitor many stars (typically 5000) at a 20 Hz cadence in order to detect serendipitous occultation events. TAOS II is operating three 1.3 m telescopes at San Pedro Martir Observatory in Baja California, Mexico. Each telescope is equipped with a custom 88 Mpix CMOS camera, capable of reading out up to 12,000 sub-frames around our target stars at a cadence of 20 Hz. TAOS II began survey operations in 2025 September, and has already collected over 60,000 star-hours of high-cadence photometry. In this presentation, the performance of the TAOS II system will be discussed.

Items.Authors: Genevieve Markees, Stephen S. Eikenberry, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Miguel Bandres, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Sergio Leon-Saval, Laurent Pueyo, Raphaël Pourcelot
Items.Title: Performance simulations of photonic-enabled exoplanet spectroscopic sensor (PEEPSS) for HWO
Items.Abstract: Technology development for the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), particularly coronagraph wavefront measurement and control, remains key for achieving the high contrast imaging and spectroscopy needed to search for and characterize exoplanets. We present simulations of the Photonic-Enabled ExoPlanet Spectroscopic Sensor (PEEPSS), a combined wavefront sensor and science channel which uses a set of photonic lanterns to couple light from the dark hole in the coronagraph focal plane into single-mode fibers and the spectrograph. PEEPSS uses rejected host starlight to aid in wavefront sensing; performing the sensing in the coronagraph focal plane helps eliminate non-common-path errors between the wavefront sensing and science channels. Initial simulations show the lanterns have high coupling efficiency (>=90%) to both the dark hole and off-axis PSFs fed through a simulated coronagraph. Each lantern also acts as a spatial modal filter, aiding in the rejection of unwanted starlight.

Items.Authors: David E. Chandler
Items.Title: Performance verification of a laser guide star jitter correction tip tilt platform
Items.Abstract: The future Ultimate-GLAO upgrade to the Subaru telescope includes a Laser Guide Star Facility (LGSF) to generate artificial guide stars that are used to measure high order wavefront error at the telescope foci. The LGSF utilizes a Tip/Tilt Mirror (TTM) based correction system to remove jitter components from the projected guide stars. The Jitter correction system incorporates high speed, two axis, piezo platforms (PI S-330.2SL piezo platform and PI E-727.xF controller). The proposed control system architecture makes use of the recently introduced EtherCAT interface of the PI E-727 controller.     The PI E-727 controllers’ performance was verified for the maximum frequency of EtherCAT commands responded too, the latency of the response and consistency of this latency with respect to the EtherCAT command.   This poster presents the results of the controller’s frequency and latency evaluation.

Items.Authors: Rion Takahashi, Hayato Takakura, Yutaro Sekimoto, Junji Inatani, Frederick Matsuda, Shugo Oguri
Items.Title: Phase-retrieved antenna patterns for space CMB telescopes equipped with a bolometer array
Items.Abstract: Future space-borne telescopes operating at 5 K and equipped with thousands of bolometers are being developed for CMB polarimetry. To characterize the antenna patterns for each detector, including far sidelobes at −60 dB level, we have studied a two–phase-step phase-retrieval method “PSH-id” (R. Takahashi et al. 2024. SPIE. 13102. 663-676). Applying this method to a scaled LiteBIRD prototype antenna - a crossed Dragone antenna with a 100 mm aperture - at 140-220 GHz, we demonstrated that the differences between the far sidelobes derived from the retrieved field and those obtained from vector near-field measurements below −60 dB.  We present the accuracy of the proposed method by comparing it with other phase-retrieval techniques. We also demonstrate its applicability at 330-500 GHz and on a 200 mm-aperture antenna. From these results, we discuss the factors that affect its accuracy and the systematic effects to which it is more susceptible compared with vector near-field measurements.

Items.Authors: Yoo Jung Kim, Michael P. Fitzgerald
Items.Title: PLsim and PLred: simulation and data-reduction/image-reconstruction software for photonic mode-based imaging
Items.Abstract: Spatial-mode-based imaging is an unconventional yet promising technique for accessing spatial information below the diffraction limit, by measuring light in a spatial-mode basis rather than in detector pixels. We present PLsim and PLred, open-source Python packages for modeling and interpreting such measurements implemented with photonic lanterns (PLs). PLsim translates astronomical scenes into PL observables, given the telescope aperture, wavefront aberrations, mode geometries, and the mode-to-channel transfer matrix; an optional photonic integrated circuit backend enables exploration of reconfigured measurement bases. Conversely, PLred recovers astronomical scenes from PL measurements. It provides an instrument-agnostic postprocessing and image reconstruction framework based on the response-map method validated on-sky. We present example use cases for Subaru/FIRST-PL, both for predicting signals with PLsim and for recovering astronomical scenes with PLred.

Items.Authors: Antoine Mérand
Items.Title: PMOIRED: recent and future developments in interferometric data modeling
Items.Abstract: With nearly 50 papers published in its first 5 years, PMOIRED has been embraced by a substantial fraction of the infrared/visible interferometric community for modeling their data and deriving astrophysical information. Flexibility, ease-of-use and seamless integration of instrumental effects make it the ideal tool for newcomers.    I will review the newest features introduced in the past couple of years, including simultaneous fits of ancillary data (e.g. photometry, spectroscopy, etc.), time variable parameters, self-calibration, bandwidth smearing, etc. These new features (which I will illustrate with published results) follow the observational trends such as the generalization of spectro-interferometry or the widespread adoption of off-axis fringe tracking.     Finally, I will present development prospects rooted in incorporating newly characterized instrumental effects, supporting new modes and developing modeling tools for new science cases.

Items.Authors: H. Philip Stahl, Christopher Hopkins, Tomasz Lis, Stephen Cheney, Ron Eng, Ernest Wright
Items.Title: POEMM optical telescope assembly design and performance verification test plan
Items.Abstract: POEMM (Planetary Origins and Evolution Multispectral Monochromator) Pioneer balloon mission requires a 1.8-m aperture optical telescope assembly (OTA) with diffraction limited performance of 70 micrometers (or better). This paper describes how the OTA is designed to meet the performance specification as a function of operating temperature and elevation angle, and for easy assembly/disassembly in Antarctica. This paper also reviews environmental test plans for the primary mirror, integrated telescope and payload in MSFC’s Center for Mirror System Characterization and Acceptance Testing.

Items.Authors: Emory L. Jenkins, A. J. Eldorado Riggs, Stuart B. Shaklan, Ewan S. Douglas
Items.Title: Polarization aberration modeling of black silicon apodizer masks
Items.Abstract: Diffraction artifacts from aperture segmentation will degrade contrast well above the 10^-10 requirement of the Habitable Worlds Observatory coronagraph instruments. Shaped pupil coronagraphs can theoretically meet this contrast by extinguishing select pupil regions while passing the rest. JPL developed reflective aluminum-coated silicon masks cryo-etched to produce black silicon, a highly absorptive metamaterial. The Roman Space Telescope will flight-qualify these masks at ~10^-8 contrast. Achieving 10^-10 contrast may require mask features only a few wavelengths wide, where mask optical behavior becomes anisotropic and polarization aberrations at reflective–absorptive boundaries cause leakage. We use FDTD simulations to characterize polarization aberrations induced by black silicon masks. We then estimate the resulting contrast degradation, establishing a lower limit on feature size and beam diameter, and explore geometry-tuning strategies to minimize polarization-induced leakage.

Items.Authors: Adrien Girardot, Coralie Neiner, Jean-Michel Reess, Olivier Dupuis, Juan Larruquert, Paloma López-Reyes, Alejandro García-Cañas
Items.Title: Pollux UV & FUV polarimeters: first lab results
Items.Abstract: The Pollux instrument for the HWO space mission has five spectropolarimetric channels, including three in the UV. UV polarimeters working on a wide wavelength range in the UV have never flown. Using a dedicated vacuum test bench, we present the first experimental results for a broadband NUV and MUV transmissive polarimeter, confirming its expected performance and increasing its Technology Readiness Level. For the FUV [100-123 nm] reflective polarimeter of Pollux, initial integration tests validate the design and demonstrate the feasibility of high-precision FUV spectropolarimetry.   This work provides the first laboratory validation of Pollux UV polarimeters and establishes a framework for testing FUV polarimeters for space applications.

Items.Authors: Yahel Sofer Rimalt
Items.Title: Precision alignment of off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror relays with concentric slide mounts: laboratory demonstration in the G-CLEF @ Magellan front end
Items.Abstract: Modern astronomical instruments use ever smaller pixels and fibers, making diffraction-limited, high-throughput relay optics essential for preserving resolution and coupling efficiency. Off-axis parabolic mirrors (OAPs) offer achromatic, diffraction-limited performance, high throughput, and unobscured pupils, but their alignment is notoriously difficult: position and angle are strongly coupled, making beam pointing and pupil walk hard to control. Conceptual “concentric” OAP mounts have been proposed to address this, but without a complete, instrument-level implementation. We implement this idea by designing, manufacturing, and testing a practical kinematic slide mount that keeps the OAP referenced to its parent paraboloid while steering the collimated beam in a single direction and eliminating OAP clocking. We deploy this mount in the seeing-limited front end of the G-CLEF spectrograph at the Magellan telescope, where dual 30° OAP relays convert F/11 to F/3.

Items.Authors: Luca Marafatto, Paolo Cerpelloni, Davide Greggio, Matteo Aliverti, Edoardo Bellone de Grecis, Maria Bergomi, Marco Bonaglia, Elena Carolo, Mirko Colapietro, Simone Doniselli, Antony Galla, Enrico Pinna, Oleksandra Rebrysh, K.K.R. Santhakumari, Brian Taylor, Valentina Viotto, Francois Rigaut
Items.Title: Precision in motion: aligning MAVIS AOM Modules from multiple sites
Items.Abstract: The MAVIS Adaptive Optics Module (AOM) integrates multiple independently developed subsystems—PFR, NGSWFS, LGSWFS, and RTC—into a single opto-mechanical assembly requiring a common optical reference. The AOM AIV strategy combines mechanical and optical methods. The PFR bench defines the mechanical and optical backbone; after shipment, modules undergo metrology checks to verify internal alignment of the module. Optical alignment uses a single telescope, with the PFR and WFS modules equipped with LOS reference targets observable with the same tool, registering all subsystems to the PFR axis. This minimizes alignment errors, simplifies on-site integration, and ensures reproducibility after transport. The paper details references, tools, sequencing, and how mechanical verification and optical LOS recovery achieve required AOM alignment accuracy.

Items.Authors: Surangkhana Rukdee, Sirinrat Sithajan, Daniel P. Sablowski, Katja Poppenhaeger, Pakakaew Rittipruk
Items.Title: Preliminary design of VIOLA: Vipa Instrument for Oxygen Loaded Atmospheres
Items.Abstract: Understanding the chemical composition of exoplanet atmospheres is essential for identifying habitable worlds and potential biosignatures. Current challenges include weak atmospheric signals from small exoplanets due to telluric contamination, spectral overlap, and limited resolution. To address this, we are developing VIOLA (Vipa-based Instrument for Oxygen Loaded Atmospheres), a compact, high-throughput, ultra-high-resolution spectrograph targeting the J and H bands in a single exposure, with an additional channel for stellar monitoring. Using a Virtually Imaged Phased Array (VIPA) as its primary disperser, VIOLA reaches R = 300,000, enabling detection of molecules such as O₂, CH₄, CO₂, CO, H₂O, OH, and HCN around nearby M-dwarfs' small planets. We present the instrument concept, preliminary optical design, and sensitivity simulations, along with plans to deploy a prototype on a 2-m telescope and scale to an 8-m facility, paving the way for future atmospheric characterization.

Items.Authors: Laure Ciesla, Marc Sauvage, C. Darren Dowell, Jochem Baselmans, Charles M. Bradford, David L. Clements, Giulia Conenna, Anne Costille, Shahab Dabironezare, Lorenza Ferrari, Johan D. Floriot, Pierre-Antoine Frugier, Jason Glenn, Renaud Goullioud, Willem Jellema, Fabrice Madec, Alexandra Mavropoulou, Tony Pamplona, Chris Pearson, Michael Peel, Edward T. Polehampton, Thomas Prouvé, Daan Roos, Sebastian Oliver, Johannes Staguhn
Items.Title: PRIMA: modeling the expected performance of PRIMAger
Items.Abstract: PRIMA is an actively cooled infrared observatory designed to provide the astrophysics community with mid- to far-infrared coverage from 24–265 µm. Its camera, PRIMAger, features a hyperspectral mode (24–84 µm, R ≈ 8) using an LVF and a polarimetric mode with four broadband, polarization-sensitive filters. We present expected detector performance, NEP estimates, filter and LVF characterization, and optical design simulations, along with observing modes and mapping strategies. These results will guide the community in preparing guest observer proposals (75% of PRIMA’s observing time).

Items.Authors: Philippe Dierickx, Will Saunders, Gaston Gausachs, Tony Travouillon, Roland Bacon, Corentin Cudennec, Laurent Pinard, Benoît Sassolas, Vincenzo Cianniello, Simone D'Auria, Vincenzo De Caprio, Ciro Del Vecchio, Salvatore Savarese, Olga Bellido, Thomas Augusteijn, Ramón Navarro, William Sutherland, Laurane Fréour, Peter Doel
Items.Title: Progress of the design of the 12-m optical, Wide-Field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST)
Items.Abstract: The Wide-Field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) is a 12-m class, Alt-Az optical telescope providing two simultaneously available foci, 2º and 3x3 arc minutes respectively, for Multi-Object Spectroscopy (MOS) and Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS). We outline the original optical solution, report progress of the structural design, of functional and physical definitions, and of the design of high-performance coatings of the telescope optics. The telescope can be wavefront-controlled at both foci, with little if any crosstalk between MOS and IFS controls. The design provides an option for seeing reduction at the IFS field, within existing technology. With a view to minimising risks, designs build extensively on solutions implemented in ESO’s VLT and ELT programmes. The WST would be located near ESO’s Paranal-Armazones observatory.

Items.Authors: Haoran Yu, Hangxin Ji, Jun Li, Songxin Dai, Qinyang Dong, Cheng Liao
Items.Title: Progress report on the spectrograph of bi-channel with ultrawide band and high flux for MOST (SCUTUM)
Items.Abstract: We report on the development progress of the Spectrograph of bi-Channel with UlTra-wide band and high flUx for MOST (SCUTUM), a first-light instrument for the Muztage-Ata 1.93-meter Synergy Telescope (MOST). Through an modified FOSC-type optical design and dual-channel configuration, SCUTUM has achieved single-exposure spectral coverage from 310 to 1000 nm. In its current phase, the instrument supports three selectable resolution modes—R~500, R~2000, and R~5000 (using a 0.8″ slit). Recent laboratory characterization shows a measured peak instrumental efficiency (excluding slit losses and detector) exceeding 65% in the low-resolution mode (R~500) and 55% in the medium-resolution mode (R~2000). Following successful integration and comprehensive testing, SCUTUM has now passed its final acceptance review. The next major milestone is on-site installation at the MOST facility, scheduled for early 2026, after which commissioning and scientific operations will begin.

Items.Authors: Ajay Ratheesh, Irfan Kuvvetli, Michał Kossakowski, Selina R. Howalt Owe
Items.Title: Prospects for developing and characterizing a 3D-CZT Compton camera with advanced signal processing and polarimetry for MeV astrophysics
Items.Abstract: The 0.1–10 MeV band, known as the “MeV gap”, remains poorly explored due to limited instrumental sensitivity. Compton imaging offers a promising approach to overcome these challenges. This work outlines the prospects and early progress towards characterizing a cost-efficient Compton camera using advanced 3D-CZT drift-strip detectors developed at DTU Space, which provide excellent room-temperature energy resolution for next-generation MeV studies. We discuss the planned design, simulation, and experimental validation of a stacked 3D-CZT Compton telescope with emphasis on imaging and polarimetry. The azimuthal scattering angle encodes information on polarization of the photon, enabling simultaneous hard X-ray/MeV polarimetry. Extending polarimetric capabilities into the MeV regime allows direct probing of non-thermal emission mechanisms. We also highlight developments in advanced signal-processing, including neural-network-based event reconstruction and real-time interaction analysis.

Items.Authors: Thomas Gascard, Valentin Sauvage, Jón Emil Guðmundsson, Bruno Maffei, Rustam Balafendiev, Morgane Loquet Le Gall, Anaïs Besnard
Items.Title: Prototype design of an internal blackbody reference for BISOU
Items.Abstract: The CMB spectral distortions, minute variations from a pure blackbody response, encode crucial information about cosmic processes from inflation to galaxy formation, which the FOSSIL mission, currently in the second step of ESA Voyage 2050 selection process, aims at observing. The BISOU balloon mission will be demonstrating the instrument concept, a Fourier transform spectrometer carrying highly sensitive measurements of the spectral distortions, enabling the detection of y and μ components.  The FTS reference signal is provided by an internal blackbody reference, consisting of an array of absorbing elements backed by a thermally conductive plate with integrated temperature control. The present investigation focuses on the comparative analysis of two prototype design utlising broadband ultra-low reflectance absorber materials coupled with precision thermal control systems that enable homogeneous and stable temperatures within a few mK in precision over the whole reference.

Items.Authors: Jiayi E. Xu, Sarik Jeram, Shaojie Chen, Ting S. Li, Zain Azam, Adi Khandelwal, Dhruv Pandya, Mark Barnet, Suresh Sivanandam, Yixuan Cheng
Items.Title: Prototyping the next-generation spectrograph for space exploration: Digital Micromirror Device based Multi-object Spectrograph (DMD-MOS) calibration and performance assessment
Items.Abstract: Abandoning the traditional approaches to multi-object spectrographs, DMD-MOS (Digital Micro-mirror Device-based Multi-Object Spectrograph) leverages a robust, elegant approach for mask creation. DMDs are arrays of microscopic flat mirrors where each micro-mirror can be addressed to selectively flip between two discrete angles. With this in mind, we have designed two optical channels for DMD-MOS - one for each of these two discrete positions: 1) an imaging channel that can be used for multi-object target selection and 2) a spectrograph channel. In this work, we present the results of our laboratory testing of DMD-MOS including spectral resolution, line spread function, wavelength coverage, and the mapping between the DMD and imaging channel planes, the latter of which enables DMD-MOS and our control software to instantaneously configure the DMD to observe the chosen target(s) in the acquisition field.

Items.Authors: Sarik Jeram, Shaojie Chen, Mark Barnet, Zain Azam, Jiayi E. Xu, Aditya Khandelwal, Ting Li, Suresh Sivanandam, Xuefeng Yao, Dhruv Pandya, Chris Cheng, Daksh Singh
Items.Title: Prototyping the next-generation spectrograph for space exploration: DMD-Based Multi-Object Spectrograph Instrument Control and On-Sky Performance
Items.Abstract: Digital Micro-mirror Device Multi-Object Spectrograph (DMD-MOS) is a multi-object, visible (400-700 nm) spectrograph that uses a Texas Instruments DLP70000 DMD as a programmable slit mask located at telescope focus to steer light into one of two channels: 1) an imaging channel used for target acquisition and slit-mask creation and 2) a traditional spectrograph. In this work, we provide an overview of the control scheme of the instrument and how both channels are used together to prepare for science observations, the PypeIt-based data reduction pipeline we have developed for DMD-MOS, and an analysis of our on-sky performance. Through this work, we highlight the importance of DMDs for next-generation multi-object spectrographs for both ground- and space-based facilities.

Items.Authors: Caimin McKenna, David Murphy, Alexey Uliyanov, Lorraine Hanlon
Items.Title: P-Terphenyl scintillator for use in a CubeSat based Compton polarimeter
Items.Abstract: Despite more than 50 years of theory and observation since the discovery of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), the composition of their relativistic jets and the processes of energy dissipation and radiation in these powerful, short-lived events are poorly understood. Gamma-ray polarimetry is a powerful diagnostic that can be used to probe these processes, and can discriminate between current models of GRB physics.     Here we present two concepts for a CubeSat-based Compton polarimeter composed of p-terphenyl detector modules as the scattering layer. These detectors make use of flight proven readout systems composed of OnSemi J-series SiPMs and the IDEAS IDE3380 SIPHRA ASIC. Laboratory measurements of energy resolution and position resolution are presented. These results are incorporated into a high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulation to assess the polarimetric performance of a representative CubeSat instrument which pairs the proposed p-terphenyl modules with a high-TRL calorimeter.

Items.Authors: Rebeka Gy Kiss, Bendegúz Koncz, Viktor L. Tóth, Gábor Battistig
Items.Title: Qualification of NIR LEDs for space use
Items.Abstract: On-board infrared calibration sources are essential for space telescopes, but traditional thermal emitters require high power and impose significant heat loads on cryogenic instruments. NIR LEDs offer a low-impact alternative that enables simpler calibration-unit designs suitable for integration near cryogenic detectors. As future infrared astronomy and space instrumentation increasingly rely on highly stable detectors, qualified NIR LED sources will become important for meeting strict calibration requirements. Although Euclid demonstrated the feasibility of LEDs in the 940-1870 nm range, their behaviour under cryogenic, radiation and long-duration conditions still require further characterization to meet space-qualification requirements defined by ESA standards. Selected 700-2500 nm LEDs are characterised through spectroradiometric, radiometric, stability and environmental testing, providing data that will support the qualification of LED-based calibration sources for future missions.

Items.Authors: Jason Patrou, Roger Angel, Chad Bender, Richard W. Wortley, William Thompson, Leroy Innecken-call, Trevor Dugan, Andrew Monson, Erich Bugueno, James Dibelka
Items.Title: Rapid and low-cost prototyping and integration strategies for the LFAST Telescope prototype
Items.Abstract: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope is a low cost and scalable optical array that replicates multiple identical 76 cm unit telescopes for visible and near infrared spectroscopy. The hardware team uses rapid prototyping with in-house 3D printed parts, water jet components, and designs intentionally optimized for low cost production. Rigorous testing informs immediate design improvements, allowing fast evolution of mechanical and thermal subsystems. Numerous multipurpose jigs and fixtures support subsystem bonding, mirror preparation, handling, and testing, including mirror support hardware and whiffle-tree assemblies for polishing, grinding, and 4D interferometer work. These methods reduce dollars per photon and support efficient mass assembly.

Items.Authors: Jianxin Chen, Teng Xu
Items.Title: Real-time controlled adaptive optics system: experimental research on wavefront reconstruction for small telescope applications
Items.Abstract: The performance of ground-based telescopes is constrained by wavefront aberrations caused by dynamic atmospheric turbulence even for small-aperture telescope . Adaptive optics systems represent the key technology for correcting such aberrations and restoring imaging quality, centred on high-speed, high-precision wavefront measurement and reconstruction, alongside the requisite real-time closed-loop control. This study aims to validate the efficacy of a real-time control system in wavefront processing and closed-loop correction for small telescopes.The system employs a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor as its core detection device, utilising a microlens array to perform subaperture segmentation and gradient measurement of the incident wavefront. Concurrently, it adopts the Fried model—widely used in regional methods for Shack-Hartmann wavefront detectors—to generate control signals in real time, thereby driving a high-speed continuous deformable mirror.

Items.Authors: Deepa Muraleedharan, Johann Hirzberger, Jan Staub
Items.Title: Real-time onboard front-end processing pipelines for PMI/Vigil: accumulation, calibration, and polarimetric demodulation for solar magnetic field measurements
Items.Abstract: The ESA Vigil mission will monitor solar activity from Lagrange point L5 to support space-weather forecasting and heliophysics research. Its Photospheric Magnetic field Imager (PMI) generates filtergrams that exceed the available telemetry, requiring real-time onboard data reduction. PMI employs FPGA-based processing to convert raw images into calibrated, demodulated science products within strict latency and resource limits. This paper describes the front-end pipeline - Accumulator and Pre-processing modules, which transform filtergrams into calibrated polarimetric spectral line profiles through deterministic, parallel execution. Subsequently, they can be transformed into physical parameter maps. Initial results reported at EDHPC (2025) and ADASS (2025) demonstrated real-time throughput and bit-accurate performance. This contribution extends those findings with updated implementations and ongoing enhancements intended to increase the scientific quality and robustness of mission data.

Items.Authors: Harrison M. Bradley, Brock Parker, Ethan Potthoff, Peter Milne, Erika Hamden, Kélian Sommer, Jacob Vider
Items.Title: Recommissioning of the Super-LOTIS remote telescope for enhanced Near UV detection
Items.Abstract: For over two decades, the Livermore Optical Transient Imaging System (LOTIS) and its successor, Super-LOTIS has remotely observed transient objects at optical wavelengths at Kitt Peak National Observatory (KPNO). However, as similar systems have come online in that time, we now wish to adapt Super-LOTIS to track in a much less observed regime: the Near UV. In this proceeding we will discuss the progress of retrofitting and updating our telescope system to that end. This process includes the commissioning of a new Teledyne Princeton Instruments SOPHIA XO camera system coated for enhanced sensitivity in NUV down to 320 nm (the atmospheric cutoff for ground-based observing). Once completed, this system will allow us to quickly and regularly follow up on UV transients identified by survey missions like Swift UV/Optical Telescope (UVOT) and Vera C. Rubin’s (VRO) Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

Items.Authors: Shugo Oguri, Frederick Matsuda, Kimihide Odagiri, Yutaro Sekimoto, Toyoaki Suzuki, Hayato Takakura, Rion Takahashi, Karen Tateoka
Items.Title: Reflectivity characterization of infrared-suppressing coated reflector surfaces for future space-borne CMB telescopes using an open Fabry–Pérot resonator
Items.Abstract: Future space-borne CMB polarization missions require stronger suppression of infrared (IR) radiation, which increases detector loading without contributing to the science signal. Conventional IR-blocking approaches using metal-mesh and absorber filters are effective but increasingly demanding, and adding additional filters introduces potential stray-light risks. As a complementary method, we investigate the possibility of suppressing IR power directly at reflector surfaces using surface-treated aluminum reflectors, including black-anodized coatings. To evaluate their millimeter-wave reflectivity and loss, we plan to measure the mirror loss over a frequency range broader than the LiteBIRD band (34-448 GHz) using an open plano–concave Fabry–Pérot–type resonator. By analyzing the S21 response and resonant Q-values, the loss of candidate materials is estimated. We present resonator design and demonstration results at 150 and 500 GHz.

Items.Authors: Angela Dora Vittoria Di Virgilio
Items.Title: Ring laser for space application
Items.Abstract: Large-frame Ring Laser Gyroscope (RLG) that provides absolute rotation measurements through the Sagnac effect have reached top sensitivity. Extisting monolithic RLG have already demonstrated prad/s sensitivity in 1 second measurement, sensitivity extremely important for space applications, mainly to improve navigation and pointing precision. Certainly large monolithic RLG structture cannot be integrated inside spacecraft. The question is whether hetero-lithic (HL) RLG can be applied to that purpose.   The project XRIstel is developing the integration of RLG for space application. The first point is the design of the HL structure, our latest HL prototype TRIO is now under test, it combines high rotational sensitivity with a modular, scalable architecture, design developed with the experience gainged from porevious prototypes. It has a square optical cavity with 6m perimeter. Results of TRIO test will be reported.

Items.Authors: Matteo Lombini, Fausto Cortecchia, Emiliano Diolaiti, Yves Magnard, Sylvain Rochat, Laura Schreiber, Eric Stadler, Stéphane Curaba, Gaële Barbary, Anne Costille, Adriano De Rosa, Kjetil Dohlen, Markus Feldt, Markus Kasper, Samuel Lévêque, Giuseppe Malaguti, Didier Maurel, Gianluca Morgante, Filomena Schiavone, Olivier Boebion, Gaël Chauvin, Florian Ferreira, Raffaele Gratton, Maud P. Langlois, Miska Le Louarn, Magali Loupias, Johan Mazoyer, Julien Milli, David Mouillet, Mamadou N'Diaye, Alain Spang, Alessandro Tacchini, Michel Tallon, Fabrice Vidal, François Wildi, Gérard Zins, Anthony Boccaletti
Items.Title: SAXO+, the second-stage adaptive optics for SPHERE+: global alignment on the SPHERE bench
Items.Abstract: SAXO+ is the second-stage Adaptive Optics module developed for the SPHERE upgrade at the ESO VLT. This work focuses on the laboratory integration and alignment of the system, carried out before its installation on the SPHERE bench. SAXO+ operates downstream of the existing SAXO XAO system and includes a switchable bypass that inserts the new optical path while preserving compatibility with the instrument. The laboratory alignment establishes the internal geometry of the relay optics, deformable mirror, and wavefront sensor, using dedicated metrology references and motorized actuators to recover the nominal pupil and focal-plane positions. Once installed at the telescope, a residual global misalignment with respect to the SPHERE optical axis may remain; this will be corrected using internal and SPHERE-level observables, as well as manual actuators on the SAXO+ mounting legs. This paper outlines the alignment methodology and integration strategy.

Items.Authors: Takanori Sakamoto, Yuta Kawakubo, Hsien-Chieh Shen, Hiro Otsuka, Ryota Kamimura, Shinpei Kubodera, Yuki Sato, Taiji Hayashi, Takumi Maeyama
Items.Title: Search for an electromagnetic counterpart of a gravitational wave source by 6U CubeSat SEAGULL
Items.Abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy revolutionizes our understanding of energetic astronomical phenomena, such as neutron star mergers. To go beyond, we need dedicated electromagnetic counterpart searches for gravitational wave events. We propose a 6U cubesat, SEArching origin of Gravitational wave source by 6U sateLLite (SEAGULL), to specialize in searching for X-ray counterparts of gravitational wave events. The mission component consists of 2 x 2 micro-pore optics and a large-format CMOS image sensor. The spacecraft bus has a solar array drive assembly (SADA) to point to any part of the sky while maintaining sufficient power to operate the spacecraft. To provide an immediate response after a gravitational wave event, we plan to use a commercial satellite network service (e.g., Inmarsat) to upload the command promptly. We aim to launch SEAGULL at the start of the next gravitational wave observing run, O5 (2029-2030).

Items.Authors: Taro Matsuo, Michael Ireland, Gautam Vasisht, Satoshi Ikari, Hirotaka Kondo, Takumi Ogawa, Masaki Ito, Satoshi Itoh, Hidehiro Kaneda, Reiki Kojima, Keita Yoshida, Tsubasa Hibi, Rashied Amini, Israel Vaughn, Warrick Schofield, Chathura Bandutunga, Toshikazu Hashimoto, Saki Nohara, Satomi Katayose, Oliver Pitz, Rachel Grange, Adrian Glauser, Sascha P. Quanz, Motohide Tamura, Chas Beichman
Items.Title: SEIRIOS: a CubeSat Formation-Flying Interferometer for in-orbit fringe measurement
Items.Abstract: SEIRIOS is a formation-flying space interferometer consisting of two 6U CubeSats and a 50-kg-class nanosatellite in low Earth orbit, designed to coherently combine light from astronomical targets. The mission, which has been approved by JAXA and is planned for launch in January 2031, aims to demonstrate millimeter-level control of three-satellite formation flying and to stabilize the optical path difference (OPD) to one hundred nanometers, enabling visible-light fringe detection. This in-orbit demonstration is a critical step toward future space interferometry missions for the direct detection of exoplanets, such as the Large Interferometer for Exoplanets (LIFE).  This presentation will introduce the SEIRIOS instrument suite, describe how high-precision fringe measurements are achieved in orbit, and outline the pathway from SEIRIOS toward future LIFE-like exoplanet missions.

Items.Authors: Declan Baker
Items.Title: Simons Observatory: design of a calibrating wire grid to measure detector polarization orientations for the Large Aperture Telescope
Items.Abstract: The cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides a detailed probe into the composition and evolution of the Universe. An extension to the standard model of cosmology suggests that light traveling cosmological distances through the Universe could result in a possible, small rotation of the CMB’s polarization plane, this is called cosmic birefringence. This effect would originate from a new parity-violating particle. The signal from cosmic birefringence is indistinguishable from the contaminant induced by systematics within the telescope. The Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) is a 6-meter millimeter wave telescope, dedicated to the study of the cosmic microwave background in intensity and polarization. In order to calibrate the Large Aperture Telescope, I have designed a rotating wire grid mounted in front of the LAT receiver to provide a reliable tool for measuring per detector absolute polarization orientation. It can be used to constrain cosmic birefringence.

Items.Authors: Richard M. McDermid, Trevor Mendel, Giovanni Cresci, François Rigaut, Jesse Cranney, Laura Magrini, Yifan Mai, Antonino Marasco, Silvia Martocchia, Davide Massari, Stephanie Monty, Gabriella Quattropani, Matteo Ceci
Items.Title: Simulating key science capabilities of the MCAO-Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph (MAVIS) on the VLT
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (Multi-conjugate adaptive-optics Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a new facility instrument for the ESO VLT due to come online in the early 2030s, uniquely providing wide-field, diffraction-limited angular resolution at visible wavelengths. In this contribution, we will review the broad science capabilities of MAVIS, focussing on a suite of detailed simulations that test the application of MAVIS to key science cases, assessing the instrument’s performance against requirements and science goals while capturing as much of the instrument design and expected behaviour as possible, such as throughput, sampling, and spatial PSF variability. Capabilities tested will include detailed astrometry for the detection of intermediate mass black holes, deep imaging of galaxies, and resolved spectroscopy of extragalactic star clusters.

Items.Authors: Felix Hagemann, Robin Anthony-Petersen, Steven E. Boggs, Emily Broadbent, Valentina Fioretti, Julian Gerber, Sophia E. Haight, Carolyn A. Kierans, Matthew G. Lassiter, Alexander Lowell, Brent Mochizuki, Samer Al Nussirat, Parshad Patel, Jarred Roberts, Nicole Rodriguez Cavero, Field Rogers, Clio Sleator, John A. Tomsick, My-Tien Tran, Aravind Valluvan, Andreas Zoglauer
Items.Title: Simulating the detector response for the COSI mission
Items.Abstract: The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) NASA Small Explorer (SMEX) mission is a Compton telescope designed to study astrophysical sources in the 0.2-5 MeV soft-gamma ray sky and planned for launch in 2027. COSI is equipped with 16 high-purity germanium cross-strip detectors which provide excellent energy resolution and the 3D-position reconstruction required for Compton event reconstruction.    Here, we present the COSI SMEX detector effects engine (DEE), a fast simulation framework to model the intrinsic detector response, from Monte Carlo energy deposits to data-like ASIC outputs. It is based on detailed detector and electronics simulations using SolidStateDetectors.jl and ngspice. To benchmark its performance, the DEE output is processed with the same analysis pipeline as the real data. We report on the current status of the DEE along with first benchmarking results with ground calibration data.

Items.Authors: Philipp Stöcker, Phil Uttley, Roland den Hartog, Erik Jan Bootsma-Mazee, Emily van Hese, Shashanth Sriramanathan
Items.Title: Simulating X-ray interferometric observations
Items.Abstract: X-ray Interferometry (XRI) promises to achieve angular resolutions below 100 µas with a maximum baseline of ~1 m on a single spacecraft, enabled by the compact telephoto optical design introduced by Willingale (2004).  Here we describe the approach of simulating XRI observations, beginning with source photon sampling, followed by simulation of the optics and the generation of interferometric fringes in the detector plane through single-photon processing, and concluding with image reconstruction using the inverse Fourier transform of the interferogram. The simulator handles inputs ranging from simple brightness distributions to spectral data cubes from advanced source models.  To accelerate image reconstruction, detected photons can be binned in spatial frequencies, which is shown to affect the quality of reconstructed interferometric images only marginally. In the low-count regime, we demonstrate that periodogram averaging techniques enable fast fringe detection.

Items.Authors: Samantha G. Morrison, Pradip Gatkine, Michael Fitzgerald
Items.Title: Simulation and development of astrophotonic H-band nulling beam combiner for the CHARA Array
Items.Abstract: Nulling interferometry is an emerging method for direct detection and characterization of faint stellar companions. Instrument performance is limited by systematic instrumental noise, which degrades the interferometric null depth and can mimic an exoplanet signal. On-chip instruments support self-calibrating architectures to address this issue.    The Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array is equipped with the world’s longest baseline in the NIR. Nulling at CHARA will require existing adaptive optics and fringe tracking facilities to be supplemented by on-chip active phase control.     Simulation suites quantify the scientific potential of new instruments. In this paper, we present our end-to-end simulator of an H-band, self-calibrated astrophotonic nulling beam combiner with active phase control for the CHARA Array. We show that the photonic nuller can detect and characterize many stellar companion systems.

Items.Authors: Yuqing Chen, Grant A. Hampson, John D. Bunton, David Humphrey, Keith J. Bengston, Guillaume Jourjon, Andrew B. Bolin, Giles C. Babich, Bernardo Bacic, Hariharan Krishnan
Items.Title: SKA low correlator and beamformer systems engineering and project management: delivery to AA2 and AA*

Items.Authors: Richard G. Dekany, Mitsuko Roberts, Reed Riddle, Randy Bartos, Jennifer Roberts, Rishi Pahuja, Dan McKenna
Items.Title: Slit spectroscopy performance gains with all-sky LGS enhancement with SIGHT
Items.Abstract: SIGHT will provide all-sky (NGS-free) LGS AO seeing enhancement for Next Generation Palomar Spectrograph (NGPS), the newly commissioned workhorse visible spectrograph for the 5m telescope at Palomar Observatory. Aligning with future AO developments at Keck Observatory, such as the K1AOF, we are developing SIGHT with modalities support high-throughput transient characterization based on minimal acquisition time, high optical transmission, and robust operations in all seeing conditions.

Items.Authors: Reed L. Riddle
Items.Title: SNORT: progress on The Spectroscopic Network Of Robotic Telescopes conceptual design
Items.Abstract: The Spectroscopic Network Of Robotic Telescopes (SNoRT) is a concept to design a light weight, low cost, custom designed, multiple mirror 3m spectroscopic telescope that is easily replicable, and then use that telescope as the template to build a worldwide network of telescopes to expand the ground based capacity for spectroscopic observations. The plan is to install eighteen telescopes at six sites spread around the world. This will fill the need for the flood of candidate targets coming from time domain surveys, as well as allow for continuous observations of objects, or larger surveys that require a lot of telescope time. The conceptual phase is underway, working out the design for the telescope in detail, as well as the options for a fiber fed spectrograph, the observatory station that will host several telescopes, and operational aspects of the robotic observing system. This presentation will discuss the current state of the conceptual design and plans for the future.

Items.Authors: Christian Hettlage, Phelokazi Dube, Danièl Groenewald, Rudolf Kuhn, Austun Louw, Nhlavutelo Macebele, Chaka Mofokeng, Nomzamo Makoena
Items.Title: Software for astronomy operations at the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT): successes, challenges, perspectives
Items.Abstract: With major updates to its proposal tools in place, the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT) now focuses on automated proposal submission, including AEONlib integration. Observation planning at the telescope is moving to a new Python-based application. Dashboards for metrics such as instrument overheads have been extended, and a dashboard for SALT's key performance indicators is under development. SALT's public data is being made available via Virtual Observatory tools. We present the software behind these changes, explain the technology stack used, give reasons for the choices made and take note of what has (or has not) proved to work well.

Items.Authors: A. N. Ramaprakash, Sorabh Chhabra
Items.Title: Speckle correlation-based diffraction-limited high resolution polychromatic imaging through the atmospheric turbulence using the memory effect principle for a Large Scale telescope
Items.Abstract: Imaging through a turbulent medium like the atmosphere has always been a difficult challenge. The random variations of the refractive index prevent the formation of diffraction-limited images; instead, we get a speckle image. In this work, we have given our analysis as to how we can exploit the inherent 'memory effect principle' present in the atmosphere to produce diffraction-limited results for amplitude recovery. This paper includes obtaining accurate speckle images through a simulated imaging system in the presence of atmospheric turbulence and its validation. For amplitude and phase recovery, an accurate approach has been developed and implemented using a hybrid Bispectrum- Fienup algorithm and tested against different sky backgrounds, read noise, and telescope reflectivity. The polychromatic effect of a limited bandwidth source has been introduced into the simulation and tested against different sky backgrounds and detector noises.

Items.Authors: David J. Erskine, Jerry Edelstein, Martin M. Sirk, Edward H. Wishnow
Items.Title: Spectrograph stabilization method using a single-delay interferometer on the Hale Telescope
Items.Abstract: We describe spectrograph stabilization useful when conventional mitigation techniques of vacuum tanks, thermal insulation and laser frequency comb systems are expensive, heavy, or bulky, such as spectrographs on airborne platforms, or mounted on moving telescopes. Placing a fixed-delay interferometer in series with a spectrograph forms an Externally Dispersed Interferometer (EDI) producing a uniform sinusoidal comb multiplying the input spectrum, creating moire. A new data analysis (“crossfading”) combines moire with input spectrum to stabilize the net output spectrum to wavelength drifts. Being a single-delay interferometer, this improves over prior crossfading requiring multiple delays. Testing on Hale EDI data of a ThAr spectral lamp using 6 iterations reduces 0.5 cm-1 [31 km/s] drift to 4x10^−7 cm−1 [2.5 cm/s]. The interferometer delay can wander, since the linearity of phase vs wavenumber interpolates a science feature between bracketing calibrating spectral references.

Items.Authors: Adam B. Johnson, William Thompson, Christian Marois, Christopher Mann, Olivier Lardière, Andre Fogal, Kaitlyn Hessel, Kris Caputa, Frédéric Grandmont
Items.Title: SPIDERS’ imaging Fourier transform spectrometer: optimal LQG control and high-fidelity spectral extraction for a full-field FTS behind a second stage focal plane WFS AO system
Items.Abstract: We present the 2025–2026 rebuild of the Imaging Fourier Transform Spectrometer (IFTS) for the Subaru Pathfinder Instrument for Detecting Exoplanets & Retrieving Spectra (SPIDERS). The system implements a real-time actuator-control architecture that maintains nanometer-level optical-path stability during continuous millimeter-scale scans of a Michelson interferometer. A model-based Linear–Quadratic–Gaussian (LQG) controller with a 100 kHz state observer provides predictive full-state estimates of mirror motion, enabling stable, low-noise operation across the wide scan-speed and scan-length regimes required for full-field exoplanet imaging and spectral retrieval. Interferometric data are reconstructed using a NUDFT with sparsity- and smoothness-promoting regularization for irregular OPD sampling, supporting spectral resolving powers from R5 to R20,000. The resulting spectra enable SPIDERS to identify biomarkers and characterize exoplanet atmospheric chemistry in a near-infrared range

Items.Authors: Frank U. Grupp, Hanna Kellermann, Helena Lamprecht
Items.Title: Split test scheme for a Gregorian space telescope: using computer generated holograms to split the test of the Gregorian telescope for Theon in the intermediate focus
Items.Abstract: We present a concept based on Computer Generated Holograms (CGH) that enables independent testing of the primary mirror (M1) and of the optical path from the Gregorian primary focus, through the secondary, to the final focus behind M1. Although the tests are carried out separately, the CGH configuration and a central reference system link both test lines, allowing highly accurate predictions of the overall Optical Telescope Assembly (OTA) performance. This decoupling of component tests greatly reduces schedule risk and cost. In addition, early use of both paths with the central reference enables rapid creation of CGH-based "as-built" telescope simulators, allowing instruments to be tested individually and early, without needing the OTA itself. The concept aligns with the "new paradigm" proposed by Arenberg, Grupp, and Kellermann [2020, 2022, 2024], which applies modular industrial building-block strategies to space optics to reduce complexity, cost, and risk.

Items.Authors: Takeshi Nakamori, Atsushi Takada, Shinya Sonoda, Mitsuru Abe, Kai Matsunaga, Soma Deguchi, Taiyo Sato, Sana Okumura, Haruki Onoda, Hiroki Yoneda, Haruki Iiyama, Dai Yaegashi, Shun Suzuki, Tatsuya Sawano, Yusuke Munakata, Kanaho Okamoto, Yoshitaka Mizumura, Masaki Mori, Tomohiko Oka, Kenji Hamaguchi, Junko Kushida, Kyoshi Nishijima, Shunsuke Kurosawa, Kentaro Miuchi, Toru Tanimori
Items.Title: Status of SMILE-3: MeV gamma-ray balloon experiment using an electron-tracking Compton camera
Items.Abstract: The SMILE-3 balloon mission aims to address long-standing questions in MeV gamma-ray astrophysics, including the origin of the Galactic Center diffuse emission and the “MeV excess.” Its key capability is the electron-tracking Compton camera (ETCC), which performs true event-by-event bijective imaging, determining the incident gamma-ray direction uniquely rather than as a Compton circle. Building on the successful SMILE-2+ detection of the Crab and Galactic Center, SMILE-3 ETCC incorporates major upgrades including a 3-atm CF_4 TPC, MPPC-based scintillator arrays, and a redesigned trigger logic. A first flight is planned for early 2028 to enable wide-area MeV surveys with unprecedented accuracy.

Items.Authors: Tony D. Travouillon, Hajime Ogane, Joschua Hellemeier, Richard Demers, Rob Sharp, Grace McGinness, David Chandler, Brian Taylor, Gaston Gausachs, Israel Vaughn, Juan-Pablo Haddad, Fernando Quiros, Bo Xin, Hugo Chiquito, Jesse Cranney, Noelia Martinez Rey
Items.Title: Status of the laser tomography adaptive optics design for the Giant Magellan Telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the status and progress of the design of the Laser Tomography Adaptive Optics system (LTAO) for the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT). The adaptive optics system consists of two major subsystems, a 6 laser guide star and wavefront sensors that will be fitted to the two instruments that support LTAO operation: GMTIFS and GMTNIRS.     After a revision of some key technology decisions in 2024 that take advantage of newly available camera, a prototype of the wavefront sensor and its assembly were prototyped in 2025. We will present these changes and the outcome of or prototyping effort in preparation to the final design phase that will start in 2026.

Items.Authors: Marianna Fulara, Piotr Wawer, Mateusz Sobiecki, Markus Czupalla, Mirosław Rataj, Konrad Skup
Items.Title: STOP analysis for ESA ARIEL fine guidance system instrument
Items.Abstract: The FGS instrument, built by a consortium led by the CBK PAN, will provide scientific data and guide ESA's ARIEL telescope to selected targets. It will be located at the L2 point and experiencing cryogenic temperatures at which it must maintain good optical performance. The instrument housing holds the cages and holders that support the optical elements in the correct configuration. The materials used in the design are aluminium, titanium, N-BK7 and SF6. Using STOP analysis, the influence of environmental conditions, especially extreme temperatures, on the optical performance of the instrument was checked. Displacements and deformations of the optical surfaces resulting from FEMAP/Nastran structural analyses were transferred to Ansys Zemax OpticsStudio using Matlab scripts. Parameters used for performance evaluation are line of sight, RMS spot, wavefront error, encircled energy and spectral resolution.

Items.Authors: Zhimin Ren, Haikun Wen
Items.Title: Structural design and on-site assembly of a nine-point whiffletree lifting system for high-precision large-aperture optical mirrors
Items.Abstract: Large precision optical mirrors in astronomical telescopes require safe and precise handling. This paper presents a flexible nine-point Whiffletree lifting system for mirrors with diameters ≥4 m. The system comprises a main steel frame and three flexible support arms connected via universal joints, providing six degrees of freedom to achieve uniform load distribution. Lifting claws feature rotational endpoints, with some driven by remote-controlled motors to avoid interference with mirror support points. Limit devices on the frame and internal guide rollers ensure accurate alignment. The design, on-site assembly, and empty-load verification are detailed. The system is lightweight, supports large loads, and ensures balanced forces, offering a reliable and efficient solution for handling and installing large optical mirrors.

Items.Authors: Maida Anwar, Jacopo Nanni, Federico Perini, Enrico Lenzi, Andrea Mattana, Luca Lepri, Giovanni Tartarini, Jader Monari
Items.Title: Study and design of 18GHz wideband analog optical link for the IF downlinks of INAF VLBI antennas (Medicina and Noto)
Items.Abstract: The Italian VLBI antennas of Medicina and Noto, and Sardinia Radio telescope te have recently been upgraded with Compact Tri-band Korean Receivers, enabling millimeter-wave observations up to the W-band (about 110 GHz). This new capability requires wideband optical fiber connections in the 18 GHz range with exceptionally low noise figure (NF) and high dynamic range. In radio astronomy, telescopes capture extremely faint signals, high dynamic range is critical to prevent stronger in-band interference from saturating the receiver and distorting the signal of interest. This demands exceptionally high dynamic range and low NF from all components in the signal chain, including the optical links. To meet these requirements, we investigated commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) optical link components capable of delivering the necessary performance.
